thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: sentry-ingest-error-rate > 5% for 5m (service: sentry-relay). Link: https://ops.redwood.example/alerts/1902

olivia: oncall here, acknowledging. I'm looking at relay metrics + relay logs. Paging raj and devops. :rotating_light:

raj: on it. grabbing relay logs. suspecting downstream vendor 3rdparty-obs returning 502s/429s based on preliminary traces.

maria: are exceptions missing entirely or delayed? customer reports are starting to come in.

olivia: events are not arriving in Sentry ingestion. Triage panel shows gaps in exception counts starting ~10:42 UTC. Likely gap = missing signals, not UI issue.

raj: logs snippet showing relay failures:
```
2026-03-15T10:43:12Z relay[pid=123] WARN http/http1: POST https://ingest.thirdparty-obs.com/api/v1/events -> 502 Bad Gateway
2026-03-15T10:43:12Z relay[pid=123] WARN queue: enqueue failed: downstream unavailable
2026-03-15T10:44:05Z relay[pid=123] ERROR buffer: drop event (queue full)
```

devops: confirmed lots of 5xx from obs vendor in the last 30m. Their status page: https://status.thirdparty-obs.com/incident/abc123 (reports "partial ingestion degradation").

olivia: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable local disk buffering on relay for short term, 2) fall back to backup ingestion endpoint (backup-dsn), 3) increase sampling to reduce load. Thoughts?

maria: we should do #2 + #3. fallback DSN exists for enterprise tenants, might be manual switch per-customer.

raj: to enable disk buffering (quick): set RELAY_BUFFER_ENABLED=true and restart relays. command:
```bash
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/relay RELAY_BUFFER_ENABLED=true && kubectl rollout restart deploy/relay
```

devops: rolling restart started. 3/5 relays up with buffering. watching backlog size.

olivia: paging security? may need to rotate public tokens if the vendor's auth errors are token-related. @pagerduty-bot page security-team if token rotation required.

pagerduty-bot: Incident created and paged to security-team (PD-4687).

raj: we also toggled per-tenant sampling for high-traffic customers: sample_rate=0.2 for identified tenants. That reduced egress attempts by ~60%.

maria: switched some enterprise tenants to backup-dsn where configured. For customers without backup-dsn we executed disk buffering + sampling.

devops: after fallback + buffering + sampling, 5xx rate to vendor dropped to ~0.5% and relay queue is draining. No new drop events seen in last 5m.

olivia: customer impact: missing exceptions and delayed triage. Estimated window of lost events: 10:42:10 UTC -> 11:08:22 UTC for customers without backup-dsn or buffering. We think buffered events for some customers were flushed; others hit queue full and were dropped.

maria: creating an alert to surface users with >20 missing events and sending email to their owners. Draft message: "We observed an ingestion degradation impacting error reporting between 10:42-11:08 UTC. Some events may not have been captured. We're investigating and will follow up."

raj: note to oncall: keep trace artifacts (relay logs, vendor response headers) — save to /mnt/incident/1902104567/ for postmortem.

olivia: handing off to sarah (next oncall) at 11:20 UTC. sarah please confirm acceptance and continue watch. :handshake:

sarah: accepted handoff. I'll monitor relays and vendor status page for the next 2 hours. Is there any customer who needs an SLA credit flagged?

maria: yes — customers with error reporting SLAs: acct-771, acct-992. marking for SRE billing review.

devops: vendor posted root cause: "partial outage in our auth proxy causing intermittent 502s" and ETA for full recovery unknown. We have backup plan documented.

olivia: summary so far: cause = thirdparty-obs ingestion/auth proxy degraded -> relay queue pressure -> event drops/delays. Mitigation = enable buffering, per-tenant fallback DSN, increase sampling, rolling restarts. Impact window and affected tenants documented.

sarah: will open incident doc and assign owners for postmortem (action items: improve local buffering defaults, prioritize per-tenant backup-dsn onboarding, automate failover).

incident-bot: NOTE: please acknowledge incident resolution link: https://ops.redwood.example/incidents/1902104567 - status: mitigated (watching).

maria: assigning follow-ups: @raj (logs archive), @devops (buffering rollout automation), @sarah (postmortem writeup).

sarah: thanks — taking over and will update this thread with the postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
